advisories.title: The affirmative D-056 eligibility claim rests on text the artifact neither pins nor protects
advisories.detail: eligibilityEffect asserts that D-056 Eligibility gates 2 and 3 would hold for DR-104. D-056 is named three times and pinned nowhere: it is absent from basedOn, absent from recordedInputs, and absent from the remeasurementClause's protected list, which enumerates file 08, leftover-join v2, corpus v1, naming v8 and this draft. The operative text is not reachable from pinned material either. COORD is pinned at the live value and its D-056 block names coordinator-decisions.D-056.turn2.draft.md and summarises the gates, but the gate-2 and gate-3 wording that the claim turns on — the execution-only remainder rule and the named-condition-4-obligation-with-an-owner rule — appears nowhere in COORD; I searched for both and found zero occurrences. So the sentence a coordinator would rely on when deciding whether to record depends on a standalone draft file that could move without triggering this artifact's own re-measurement.
advisories.whyItStaysAdvisory: I was close to calling this a SHOULD-FIX and the family convention is what decided it. Not one structural sibling pins the D-056 turn-2 draft: not gate-harness-naming v8 or v6, not dr117-ee-gate-naming v3, and not identity-namespace-leftover-join v2 — the artifact that commissioned this one, which mentions D-056 seven times and states the mirror-image conclusion, 'Gates 2 and 3 do not hold', with no pin at all. Holding this candidate to a standard that no artifact in its lineage meets, including its own commissioner, would be moving the bar rather than applying it. The claim is also accurate: I verified both gates against the draft's actual text, and confirmed that D-056's stated reason for listing DR-104 ineligible — that negative-test corpus authoring remains — went stale at D-130.
advisories.whatKeepsItWorthRecording: One asymmetry survives the convention argument. The siblings make negative claims about these gates; this artifact makes the affirmative one, and affirmative eligibility claims run toward a SATISFIED recording rather than away from it. That is the direction in which an unverified dependency costs more. Note also that the leftover-join family elsewhere in this corpus — the DR-105, DR-120 and DR-122 joins — does pin the D-056 turn-2 draft at dfb0c2af in basedOn, so the corpus already contains the convention that would close this.
advisories.whatWouldCloseIt: Add coordinator-decisions.D-056.turn2.draft.md with sha256 dfb0c2af39ff31df9bf3609c131f03ee2d87a585dcd684abd633d47ffb11ed82 to basedOn and recordedInputs, and name it in the remeasurementClause's protected list. The digest is already in use elsewhere in the corpus for exactly this purpose.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 advisory. Twenty-seven attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 7ff69882 at 0444, 11780 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26 and owners 30 of 30 at both ends; DR-104 token DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED as the subject states; file 08 and COORD unmodified, and DR-G31 occurs in neither, which is the evidence that this file existing is not the recording. All eight cited digests reproduce and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head. The dispatch's equality attack fails: namedElevenClassesVerbatim equals the D-130 authoredCatalog class order exactly, index by index, eleven against eleven, and the parenthetical inside the proposed file-08 harnessCell parses to the same list, so the order does not drift between the two places it appears. classCount 11 matches the corpus's classCount and primaryCount. No twelfth class is invented — notATwelfthClass quotes the corpus's own deferral verbatim, and also-bytes are expressly kept as also-bytes rather than promoted. Because this is the first subject in the sequence that proposes to enlarge required-now, I checked every limb of the act for having been performed instead of proposed: file 08 unedited with the row carrying an explicit 'Not written' standing; no D-* number and no COORD heading; the harness specification unauthored; the eleven classes unexecuted; and artifactPathWhenAuthored tested on the filesystem, absent before and after. The condition-4 arithmetic was checked against live counts rather than accepted — 26 gates and 30 owners today, 27 and 31 with one added — and both figures are right. The one claim that could have over-reached is eligibilityEffect, which says D-056 gates 2 and 3 would hold for DR-104. I tested it against D-056's actual gate text. Gate 2 requires an execution-only remainder and excludes authoring; the leftover-join's sole leftover-design entry is OBL-NT-11-EXECUTION and its authoring limb closed at D-130. Gate 3 requires the remainder to be named at a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner, which is what this candidate does, and it honours the caveat that naming is not itself SATISFIED. I also confirmed that D-056's own reason for listing DR-104 ineligible — negative-test corpus authoring remains — went stale at D-130, so the claim is not made against a live bar. It is limited to two of the five gates and disclaims the rest. Accurate. One advisory, and it is the finding I nearly filed. D-056 is named three times and pinned nowhere — not in basedOn, not in recordedInputs, and not in the remeasurementClause's protected list — and its operative text is not reachable from pinned material either: COORD is pinned and names the turn-2 draft, but the gate-2 and gate-3 wording appears nowhere in COORD, which I confirmed by searching for both. What stopped the finding was checking the family convention: no structural sibling pins that draft, not naming v8 or v6, not dr117-ee-naming v3, and not identity-namespace-leftover-join v2, the artifact that commissioned this one and states the mirror-image conclusion 'Gates 2 and 3 do not hold' with no pin at all. Holding this candidate to a bar none of its lineage meets would be moving the goalposts. What keeps it worth recording is that the siblings make negative claims where this one makes the affirmative claim, and affirmative eligibility runs toward a SATISFIED recording, which is the direction where an unverified dependency costs more — and the leftover-join family elsewhere in this corpus already pins that draft at dfb0c2af, so the convention that would close it exists. One disclosure: I opened the leftover-join v2 Codex verdict, reading only its verdict line and counts, to check a citation the subject makes about it; a coordinator reading the prohibition strictly should discount that one verification.
